title: Loose stone samples tested in Israel turn out to be basalt

tellings.quote: And basalt, volcanic stones they found.

plain: In 2012, loose stones collected from the seafloor at the Baltic Sea anomaly, a strange round shape found on the bottom of the Baltic by a Swedish treasure-hunting team, were tested in Israel and turned out to be basalt, a volcanic stone. The treasure hunter Dennis Asberg, who led the team that found it, tells Michels what the testers found: "basalt, volcanic stones." The result bears on what the object might be made of.
